# nv-codec-headers NVENC header

This directory vendors only the MIT-licensed `nvEncodeAPI.h` header from
FFmpeg's clean-room `nv-codec-headers` (`ffnvcodec`) project, so Arcen can
generate NVENC FFI bindings without redistributing NVIDIA Video Codec SDK
material.

- Upstream: https://github.com/FFmpeg/nv-codec-headers
- Tag: `n12.1.14.1`
- Tag object: `e1ff958747e9e08247cea31b6e629d61ece824c0`
- Commit: `7c8e7fc751f803c672b42c37d9199c8a4f98b327`
  (`git ls-remote` peels the annotated tag to this commit; the vendored
  header byte-matches it. The tag object hash is not the commit hash.)
- Header: `include/ffnvcodec/nvEncodeAPI.h`
- NVENC API version: **12.1**
- Upstream note: corresponds to NVIDIA Video Codec SDK 12.1; minimum driver
  versions Linux 530.41.03 or newer, Windows 531.61 or newer.
- License: MIT, reproduced in `LICENSE` and in the header preamble.

Only this header and its license notice are vendored. Do not replace it with
headers from the NVIDIA Video Codec SDK.

## Why 12.1 and not the newest tag

Pick the header by **driver compatibility, not recency**. The NVENC API version
is embedded in every struct version constant, and the driver rejects any API
newer than it supports — `NvEncOpenEncodeSessionEx` returns
`NV_ENC_ERR_INVALID_VERSION` and encoding fails completely at runtime.

This is not hypothetical. A first attempt vendored `n13.1.15.0` (API 13.1),
which compiled cleanly, passed every unit test, and then failed on the first
real GPU with exactly that error, because API 13.1 requires driver 610.0+ and
the target ran 570.172.08. Compilation proves nothing here; only a run against
a real encoder does.

API 12.1 is also the version Arcen's encoder call sites were written and
validated against, so vendoring it keeps this a purely legal change — swapping
an SDK-derived header for a clean-room one — with no behavioural difference and
no increase in the minimum supported driver.

If you raise this version, you are raising Arcen's minimum NVIDIA driver
requirement. Check the upstream `README` for the tag's minimum driver, and
verify on real hardware before merging.

## Regenerating Rust bindings

The committed Rust bindings in
`hosts/capenc/src/nvenc_sys/windows_sys/nvEncodeAPI.rs`, plus the companion
`guid.rs` and `version.rs`, are generated from this vendored header. They are
committed deliberately instead of generated in `build.rs` so Linux/Windows host
builds do not gain a libclang/build-time bindgen dependency.

Generation command used for `nvEncodeAPI.rs`:

```sh
bindgen third_party/nv-codec-headers/include/ffnvcodec/nvEncodeAPI.h \
  --allowlist-type '^(NV|_NV|PNV|GUID|_GUID|RECT|tagRECT|LONG).*' \
  --allowlist-var '^(NV|_NV).*' \
  --allowlist-function '^Nv.*' \
  --blocklist-item '^NV_ENC_.*_GUID$' \
  --rustified-enum '.*' \
  --with-derive-default --with-derive-hash --with-derive-partialeq \
  --with-derive-partialord --with-derive-eq --with-derive-ord \
  --use-core \
  --raw-line 'pub use super::super::{guid::*, version::*};' \
  --raw-line '// Generated by rust-bindgen 0.65.1 from nv-codec-headers n12.1.14.1 (MIT), commit 7c8e7fc751f803c672b42c37d9199c8a4f98b327.' \
  --raw-line '// Source header: third_party/nv-codec-headers/include/ffnvcodec/nvEncodeAPI.h; do not regenerate from the NVIDIA Video Codec SDK.' \
  -o hosts/capenc/src/nvenc_sys/windows_sys/nvEncodeAPI.rs
```

`version.rs` is transcribed by hand, because `NVENCAPI_STRUCT_VERSION` is a
function-like C macro that bindgen does not expand. After regenerating, diff the
set of `*_VER` constants against the header's `#define`s — a missing one is a
build break, and that has happened.
